scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to want to attend my great aunt's funeral. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I just found out that my great aunt Wyndy died. I've never heard of her before, and the only time I met her was when I was extremely young, like 1 or 2 years old. I don't remember anything about her, and my family hasn't mentioned her at all until now. My mom is insisting that I go to the funeral, saying it's out of respect and support for her. But I feel really awkward going to funerals, especially for people I don't know well. I'm also thinking about the family dynamics here. My mom says that this is one of the few times we'll see the larger branch of the family, and there might be hundreds of people there, but I've only seen about 10 of them more than once. It feels like I'm gate-crashing someone else's family event, and I don't think anyone would want me there since I don't know the person who died. I'm wondering if it's wrong to not want to attend just because she's family. I mean, I understand that family is important, but in this case, I feel like I don't have any connection to her or the larger family branch. It's not like we've had any meaningful interactions or shared experiences. On the other hand, my mom is emphasizing respect and support. I guess attending the funeral could be a way to show that I care about my family and their traditions. But I'm not sure if forcing myself to go would actually make me feel respectful or if it would just make me uncomfortable and resentful. I'm also thinking about the cultural aspect. In some cultures, attending funerals is a significant obligation, and not doing so could be seen as disrespectful. But in my experience, it's more about personal connections and how close you are to the person who passed away. Another thing to consider is the potential impact on my relationship with my mom. If I don't go, will she feel hurt or unsupported? I don't want to cause unnecessary tension, but I also don't want to compromise my own feelings and comfort. I'm also reflecting on whether there's a middle ground. Maybe I can find a way to show respect without attending the funeral, like sending flowers or a card. That way, I'm acknowledging the loss without putting myself in an uncomfortable situation. Overall, I'm torn between the expectation to attend family events and my personal feelings about it. I need to figure out what's more important in this situation: family obligation or my own emotional well-being.
